Principle 18: Holidays
My country has many traditional holidays.
Holidays are a special time when families can get together and celebrate.
We celebrate Lunar New Year’s, Independence Day, Arbor Day,
Buddha’s Birthday and many more.
I would like to tell you about the two largest traditional holidays in Korea.
The first big holiday is Lunar New Year’s also known as seol-lal.
The most important Lunar New Year custom is the
ancestral memorial ceremony.
Each member of the family gets up early in the morning
and dresses in their best clothes.
Afterwards, we perform a ritual ceremony in honor of our ancestors.
Following the ceremony, the younger people bow to their elders
as a gesture of wishing everyone many new blessings
during the upcoming new year.
To bow on the Lunar New Year is a special honor
and privilege of showing respect to one’s elders.
Chu-seok is the biggest national holiday of the year,
and it is often referred to as the Korean Thanksgiving.
During Chu-seok, People visit their ancestrial tombs
and make an offering of food to their ancestors.
In addition, most people play games with their relatives
and make song-pyeun, which is a Korean traditional rice cake.
I like our country's traditional holidays.
On these days I learn how important family is!
